name: REBCO high-temperature superconductors for compact tokamaks
summary: Rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO) cuprate tapes carry high currents at 20 K and above 20 T, allowing compact high-field tokamaks (SPARC, ARC) because fusion power density scales as B^4 at fixed beta; quench protection and neutron degradation of the cuprate are open engineering problems.
sources: Creely et al. (2020). "Overview of the SPARC tokamak". *J. Plasma Phys.* 86, 865860502. [doi:10.1017/S0022377820001257](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0022377820001257)

name: Dense hydrogen: superconductors and laser-shock experiments
summary: The insulator-metal transition of dense hydrogen and deuterium, the root of the metallic-hydrogen and hydride-superconductor programme, is probed both in diamond-anvil cells and in dynamic compression at NIF and the Z machine; the two disagree on the transition pressure, partly because of temperature and DFT functional choices.
sources: Knudson et al. (2015). "Direct observation of an abrupt insulator-to-metal transition in dense liquid deuterium". *Science* 348, 1455. [doi:10.1126/science.aaa7471](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaa7471)
Celliers et al. (2018). "Insulator-metal transition in dense fluid deuterium". *Science* 361, 677. [doi:10.1126/science.aat0970](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0970)

name: Band topology of magnetized plasma waves
summary: Chern numbers and bulk-boundary correspondence, developed for electronic bands, classify the wave bands of magnetized cold plasmas; a topological gaseous plasmon polariton is predicted at plasma interfaces with a sign change of B or density.
map: C_n=\frac1{2\pi}\int\Omega_n(\mathbf k)d^2k\ \text{for the Maxwell-fluid eigenproblem }\omega\psi=H(\mathbf k)\psi
sources: Parker et al. (2020). "Topological Gaseous Plasmon Polariton in Realistic Plasma". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 124, 195001. [arXiv:1911.02148](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.02148)

name: Guiding-centre drift and the Hall effect
summary: In crossed E and B fields charged particles drift at E x B / B^2 regardless of charge or mass; in a 2D electron gas this drift gives the classical Hall conductivity, and quantized cyclotron orbits (Landau levels) with skipping orbits at edges become the chiral edge states of the quantum Hall effect.

name: Primordial plasma and Thomson scattering
summary: Before recombination the universe was a tightly coupled photon–baryon plasma, whose acoustic oscillations imprint the CMB peaks. Thomson scattering off free electrons sets the optical depth, and reionization polarizes the CMB.

name: BAO as sound waves in the primordial plasma
summary: Baryon acoustic oscillations are ion-acoustic-like pressure waves in the coupled photon–baryon fluid. The sound horizon is a standard ruler, and Jeans instability parallels plasma streaming and gravitational instabilities.
breaks: Gravity and radiation drag replace electrostatic restoring forces, and there is no Debye-scale dispersion.

name: Magnetically driven AGN jets
summary: Relativistic AGN jets are launched and collimated by magnetic fields threading a black hole or disk, as in Blandford–Znajek and Blandford–Payne. These are force-free and relativistic MHD flows.

name: Reconnection in jets and coronae
summary: Relativistic reconnection and plasmoid chains are invoked for particle acceleration and fast blazar flares, and for heating accretion-disk coronae.

name: Turbulence and magnetic fields in clusters
summary: Cluster mergers and AGN drive turbulence that amplifies magnetic fields by a small-scale turbulent dynamo. Radio halos arise from turbulent reacceleration of relativistic electrons.

name: Intracluster medium as a weakly collisional plasma
summary: The hot, magnetised intracluster medium has long mean free paths, so pressure anisotropy, firehose and mirror instabilities, and suppressed Spitzer conduction require kinetic treatment. Plasma microinstabilities regulate viscosity and heat transport.

name: Reionization and the intergalactic plasma
summary: Reionization turned the neutral intergalactic medium into a tenuous, ionized plasma. Its free-electron column sets the CMB optical depth and the FRB dispersion measure.

name: Galactic dynamo and seed fields
summary: Galactic magnetic fields of microgauss strength are explained by mean-field αΩ dynamos acting on weak seed fields. Fluctuation dynamos amplify fields in early galaxies, and the seed origin remains open.

name: Astroparticle sources are astrophysical plasma shocks
summary: High-energy astrophysical sources accelerate particles in collisionless shocks and magnetised outflows, so plasma shock physics underlies cosmic-ray, GRB and neutrino source modelling.

name: Plasma wakefield acceleration and astrophysical acceleration
summary: Wakefield acceleration and cosmic-ray acceleration both push charged particles to high energy in collective plasma fields, and wakefield-type mechanisms are proposed for UHECR. Wakefields are coherent and laminar while Fermi processes are stochastic.
breaks: Wakefields give deterministic gradients in a driven wave, while Fermi acceleration is statistical scattering across a shock.

name: Alfvén waves scatter cosmic rays
summary: Cosmic rays stream along field lines and resonantly excite Alfvén waves, which scatter them and set the diffusion coefficient. Self-generated waves confine Galactic cosmic rays and feed back in shock precursors.

name: Turbulent scattering and cosmic-ray transport
summary: Cosmic-ray diffusion in the Galaxy is set by scattering off MHD turbulence. Goldreich–Sridhar anisotropy makes resonant scattering by Alfvénic modes inefficient, so compressive modes and cascade properties matter.

name: Cosmic rays and heliospheric particle physics
summary: Galactic cosmic rays propagate through the turbulent magnetised solar wind and heliosphere, where modulation, diffusion and scattering are plasma processes. The same transport theory applies in the Galaxy.

name: Diffusive shock acceleration of cosmic rays
summary: First-order Fermi acceleration at collisionless shocks yields a power-law spectrum p^-(3r/(r-1)) with index near 2 for strong shocks, and explains the cosmic-ray spectrum from supernova remnants. Magnetic-field amplification enables acceleration toward the knee.

name: FRB emission as coherent plasma processes
summary: FRB models invoke coherent emission from plasma instabilities, maser-like shock emission and magnetospheric reconnection. Propagation through plasma produces dispersion, scattering and Faraday rotation, which make FRBs probes of intergalactic baryons.

name: GRB afterglows from relativistic collisionless shocks
summary: GRB afterglow synchrotron emission arises from relativistic collisionless shocks, where Weibel-type instabilities generate magnetic fields and accelerate electrons. PIC simulations of these shocks inform the microphysical parameters ε_B and ε_e.

name: Planetary interiors at megabar pressures
summary: Giant-planet interiors contain hydrogen, helium and water at megabar pressures, where laser shock experiments measure the equation of state, metallization and demixing. Results feed interior and evolution models.

name: Magnetised accretion disks and the MRI
summary: Angular momentum transport in ionised protoplanetary disks is driven by the magnetorotational instability. Nonideal MHD effects (Ohmic, Hall, ambipolar) and disk winds set accretion and dead zones.

name: Disk MRI from ideal-MHD Alfvén dynamics
summary: The MRI is an ideal-MHD instability in which a weak field acts like a spring tying fluid elements in differential rotation, an Alfvén-wave tension effect. It drives disk turbulence and angular momentum transport.

name: Stellar interiors and atmospheres are plasmas
summary: Stars are self-gravitating plasmas. Their equation of state, opacity, transport, convection, magnetism and winds draw on plasma physics, and fusion burning links to laboratory fusion.

name: Dense matter equations of state in the lab
summary: Laser-driven shocks and X-ray Thomson scattering probe warm dense matter relevant to white-dwarf and giant-planet interiors. Laboratory equations of state calibrate dense-plasma models for compact objects.

name: Pulsar wind nebulae and relativistic shocks
summary: Pulsar winds terminate in relativistic shocks that accelerate pairs and power synchrotron nebulae such as the Crab. These are testbeds for relativistic shock acceleration and magnetic reconnection in striped winds.

name: Stellar nucleosynthesis and fusion burning
summary: Stars burn by thermonuclear fusion with Gamow-peak reaction rates, and fusion devices target the same reactions. Laboratory D-T burning plasmas are self-heated by alphas, like stellar cores.
breaks: Stars confine by gravity at about 10^7 K and long timescales, while devices use magnetic fields at 10^8 K and lack gravitational stability.

name: Rayleigh–Taylor mixing in supernovae and ICF
summary: Hydrodynamic instabilities at accelerating interfaces occur in core-collapse explosions and in ICF capsule implosions. Scaled laser experiments reproduce supernova mixing, and the shared physics is Rayleigh–Taylor and Richtmyer–Meshkov growth.
breaks: ICF has ablation stabilization and sharp interfaces, while supernovae involve gravity, neutrinos and nuclear burning.

name: Supernova remnant shocks
summary: Supernova remnants are the canonical sites of collisionless shocks, with magnetic-field amplification, thin X-ray rims and gamma-ray emission. They are the leading candidate sources of Galactic cosmic rays.

name: Solar magnetism as MHD
summary: Sunspots, flux emergence, flares and coronal structure are MHD phenomena. Frozen-in flux, reconnection and Alfvén waves describe the Sun's magnetic activity.

name: The solar dynamo and the solar cycle
summary: The 11-year solar cycle is produced by a dynamo in which differential rotation (the Ω-effect) and helical convection (the α-effect) regenerate field. Helioseismology constrains the rotation profile that feeds mean-field models.

name: Solar flares as reconnection
summary: Solar flares and CMEs release stored magnetic energy by reconnection, per the standard CSHKP model. The Sweet–Parker rate is too slow, which motivated plasmoid and collisionless reconnection.

name: Sun to heliosphere
summary: The Sun drives the solar wind, coronal mass ejections and space weather. Helioseismology and coronal physics set the boundary conditions for heliospheric plasma models.

name: Parker wind and coronal heating
summary: The corona, with its heating problem, is the base of the Parker wind. Alfvén-wave turbulence and reconnection are candidate heaters, and the transonic wind solution follows from hydrodynamic equations.

name: Strongly coupled plasma models for HED matter
summary: One-component plasma, Yukawa fluids and molecular-dynamics results from dusty and ultracold plasmas supply structure factors and transport coefficients used to interpret X-ray Thomson scattering and equations of state.

name: Warm dense matter as strongly coupled plasma
summary: Warm dense matter sits at coupling parameter Gamma of order 1 and degeneracy of order 1, the regime where one-component plasma models and dusty-plasma analogues apply. HED experiments probe this regime.

name: Alpha self-heating and ignition in ICF and MCF
summary: Both routes aim at burning plasmas dominated by alpha heating, with ignition set by alpha deposition exceeding losses. They differ in the confinement mechanism: inertia, with a rho-R criterion, versus magnetic fields, with a nTtau criterion.

name: Burning-plasma physics across confinement schemes
summary: Alpha heating, thermal-instability feedback and the Lawson criterion are shared concepts. Fuel assembly by compression is replaced by long-pulse steady confinement.
breaks: ICF burn lasts about 100 ps and is limited by hydrodynamic disassembly. MCF burn is quasi-steady and limited by transport, MHD stability and exhaust.

name: Rayleigh–Taylor instability in ICF and MHD interchange
summary: Rayleigh–Taylor growth at the ablation front and in the hot spot parallels the interchange instability, where bad field curvature acts as effective gravity.
breaks: Ablation stabilises ICF RT growth. The interchange instability is set by field-line curvature and pressure gradient, not by an acceleration.

name: Ponderomotive force in wakefields
summary: The ponderomotive force of a laser pulse expels electrons and excites the wake. Relativistic self-focusing and channeling guide the pulse.

name: Collisional absorption and ionization
summary: Collisional (inverse bremsstrahlung) heating of electrons by an oscillating field and the resulting ionization avalanche follow the same physics in RF discharges and laser-produced plasmas.

name: Parametric instabilities in laser plasmas
summary: Stimulated Raman and Brillouin scattering and two-plasmon decay are three-wave couplings of light with Langmuir and ion-acoustic waves. They limit laser coupling in ICF.

name: Wakefields as driven Langmuir waves
summary: A wakefield is a driven plasma oscillation at the plasma frequency with phase velocity equal to the driver velocity. The wave-breaking field sets the scale of the accelerating gradient.

name: Streamer and dielectric-barrier breakdown
summary: Townsend avalanche and streamer breakdown in atmospheric DBDs and jets follow the same Paschen breakdown physics as low-pressure processing discharges, but at much higher pd and collisionality.

name: Debye sheaths in processing plasmas
summary: Debye shielding sets the sheath thickness at electrodes and wafers. The Bohm criterion and Child–Langmuir law determine ion energy and flux in etching and deposition.

name: Guiding-centre drifts in toroidal confinement
summary: Grad-B and curvature drifts in a torus cause vertical charge separation, so a rotational transform is needed. Trapped-particle banana orbits arise from the mirror force and adiabatic invariants, and they set neoclassical transport.

name: Laboratory and fusion dynamo relaxation
summary: Reversed-field pinch and spheromak relaxation show a dynamo-like conversion of helicity. Stellarators avoid the dynamo by using external coils.
breaks: Stellarators are not dynamos. The mapping applies to the RFP and spheromak, not to stellarator confinement.

name: Quasi-symmetry and omnigeneity from guiding-centre motion
summary: Quasi-symmetry makes the guiding-centre Hamiltonian depend on |B| only through a symmetric combination, so a conserved canonical momentum confines particles as in a tokamak. Omnigeneity confines trapped orbits.

name: Alfvén physics in tokamaks
summary: Alfvén waves and continuum damping underlie fast-ion-driven Alfvén eigenmodes, and frozen-in flux constrains tokamak equilibria and disruption dynamics.

name: MHD equilibrium and stability of tokamaks
summary: Grad–Shafranov equilibrium, the safety factor, and kink, ballooning and interchange stability come from ideal MHD energy principles. They set the Troyon beta limit and the Kruskal–Shafranov current limit.

name: Sawteeth, tearing modes and disruptions
summary: Sawtooth crashes, neoclassical tearing modes and the thermal and current quench of disruptions involve resistive reconnection and magnetic island formation. The Kadomtsev model is a reconnection model.

name: Gyrokinetic codes for astrophysical turbulence
summary: Gyrokinetic theory built for tokamak drift waves was adapted to astrophysical plasmas, for example the Alfvénic cascade in the solar wind, using the same low-frequency anisotropic ordering.

name: Gyrokinetics from Vlasov theory
summary: Gyrokinetics is the Vlasov–Maxwell system averaged over gyro-phase using adiabatic invariants. It keeps Landau-type wave-particle resonances and drives drift-wave turbulence and zonal flows.
map: \partial_t f+\mathbf v\cdot\nabla f+\tfrac{q}{m}(\mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)\cdot\partial_{\mathbf v}f=0

name: Landau resonance in drift-wave transport
summary: Landau damping and the resonant wave-particle energy exchange set the growth and saturation of ITG and TEM modes. Collisionless zonal-flow damping, the Rosenbluth–Hinton residual, is also a kinetic effect.

name: Geodynamo as the source of the magnetosphere
summary: Earth's magnetic field, produced by the geodynamo, forms the magnetospheric cavity. Its dipole nature sets the radiation belts and the aurora geometry.

name: Solar dynamo and the heliospheric field
summary: The solar dynamo generates the cycle-varying field that the wind drags out into the Parker spiral and the heliospheric current sheet. The cycle modulates wind structure and space weather.

name: MHD waves as the low-frequency limit of plasma waves
summary: Alfvén and magnetosonic waves are the low-frequency fluid limits of the kinetic cold-plasma dispersion relation, which includes whistlers and ion cyclotron waves at higher frequency.

name: Reconnection across space plasmas
summary: Reconnection powers solar flares, coronal mass ejections and magnetospheric substorms. It also appears in the heliospheric current sheet and in particle acceleration in astrophysical sources.

name: Relativistic reconnection as particle accelerator
summary: Relativistic reconnection in pulsar winds, jets and magnetar flares accelerates non-thermal particles through X-point and plasmoid dynamics. It competes with diffusive shock acceleration.

name: Dayside and tail reconnection in the Dungey cycle
summary: Reconnection at the magnetopause and in the magnetotail drives the Dungey cycle, substorms and flux transfer events. MMS directly observed the electron diffusion region.

name: Space weather driven by reconnection
summary: Southward interplanetary magnetic field opens the magnetosphere via dayside reconnection. This loads the tail and drives geomagnetic storms.

name: Kinetic dissipation of MHD cascades
summary: At ion and electron scales the MHD cascade becomes a kinetic Alfvén wave cascade. Landau damping, in the form of transit-time damping, and cyclotron resonance remove energy, with a gyrokinetic description such as the one used in tokamaks.

name: Solar wind as an MHD turbulence laboratory
summary: In situ spacecraft measurements of solar wind fluctuations test anisotropic Alfvénic cascade theories such as Goldreich–Sridhar and critical balance. The spectrum and its kinetic-scale break are also linked to coronal heating.

name: Turbulent heating of the corona and wind
summary: Alfvén-wave turbulence cascades energy to ion-kinetic scales, where it heats ions by cyclotron or stochastic processes. This is a leading explanation for coronal and solar wind heating.

name: Streaming instabilities in shocks and cosmic rays
summary: Weibel, Bell and cosmic-ray streaming instabilities amplify magnetic fields and scatter particles at collisionless shocks, enabling diffusive shock acceleration.

name: Adiabatic invariants and radiation belts
summary: Gyration, bounce and drift motion with conserved adiabatic invariants trap particles in the van Allen belts. Violating an invariant by ULF waves or substorm injection drives radial transport and acceleration.

name: Ring current and drifts
summary: The ring current is the westward drift of ions and eastward drift of electrons, driven by gradient and curvature drifts in the dipole field. It depresses the surface field in storms, measured by Dst.

name: High-pressure equations of state for planetary cores
summary: Laser-shock and diamond-anvil experiments measure iron's equation of state and melting at core pressures, calibrating seismically inferred inner-core density and temperature.

name: Charged-particle stopping power
summary: Alpha and ion energy deposition in dense plasma and Bragg-peak dose deposition in tissue both follow Bethe-type stopping physics, with plasma screening modifying stopping in hot targets.
breaks: Free-electron collective response in plasmas changes stopping relative to bound-electron tissue.

name: Laser-driven particle and radiation sources
summary: Intense lasers in plasma drive electron and ion beams and betatron or undulator-like radiation, producing compact versions of accelerator and light-source outputs.

name: Radiation by accelerated charges
summary: Betatron radiation in plasma, relativistic Thomson scattering and undulator radiation all derive from the Liénard–Liparticle radiation formula for accelerated relativistic charges.

name: Laser-driven ion acceleration for proton therapy
summary: Target-normal sheath acceleration produces MeV-scale protons from laser-irradiated foils, targeted at Bragg-peak therapy, though current energies and reproducibility fall short.

name: Accelerator physics applied to plasma acceleration
summary: Emittance, beta-function matching, energy spread and staging from conventional beam dynamics are the figures of merit for plasma-accelerated beams.

name: Plasma wakefields as compact accelerators
summary: Plasma wakefield accelerators replace RF cavities with plasma waves sustaining GV/m gradients; beam dynamics, emittance and staging concepts from accelerator physics govern their beam quality.

name: Betatron oscillations in ion channel
summary: Beam electrons in the plasma ion-channel focusing field undergo betatron oscillations with the same envelope equations as strong focusing lattices, with focusing strength set by plasma density.

name: Plasma-driven free-electron lasers
summary: Plasma-accelerated beams and betatron emission are being used to drive FELs and X-ray sources, but the FEL's tight emittance and energy-spread demands challenge plasma beams.
breaks: Plasma beams' percent-level energy spread typically exceeds the FEL Pierce parameter tolerance.

name: Compact accelerators for radiotherapy
summary: Laser-plasma ion and electron beams are proposed as compact sources for proton therapy and FLASH radiotherapy, but stability and energy spread remain limiting.

name: Plasma processing for device fabrication
summary: Plasma etching, deposition and ion implantation-related processes pattern and build transistors and solar cells; sheath physics sets ion energy and anisotropy of etched features.

name: Plasma–surface interactions and plasma catalysis
summary: Plasma radicals and ions adsorb, react and sputter at surfaces, linking discharge physics to adsorption, surface reactions and plasma-assisted catalysis.

name: Plasma medicine and biological response
summary: Cold atmospheric plasmas deliver reactive oxygen and nitrogen species to cells and tissue, so biological sensing and response physics determines therapeutic and toxic outcomes.

name: Non-equilibrium plasma chemistry and reaction kinetics
summary: Electron-impact dissociation, vibrational excitation and radical reactions in cold plasmas follow state-resolved rate theory and potential-energy-surface concepts, with electron temperature far above gas temperature.
breaks: Rate theories assuming a single Boltzmann temperature fail when electron and gas temperatures differ strongly.

name: Surface chemistry underlying plasma etching
summary: Etch and deposition rates and selectivity are set by adsorption, ion-enhanced surface reactions and sputter yields studied in surface science.

name: Neutral beam injectors as ion accelerators
summary: Neutral beam heating of fusion plasmas relies on ion source, electrostatic acceleration and neutraliser technology developed in accelerator physics.

name: Hamiltonian field-line flow and storage-ring dynamics
summary: Magnetic field lines in toroidal devices form a Hamiltonian system with islands and KAM surfaces, as do particle orbits in storage rings with nonlinear resonances.
breaks: Field-line flow has no physical particle dynamics, and rotational transform plays the role of tune.

name: Superconducting magnets and RF technology
summary: Tokamaks and accelerators share superconducting magnet technology (Nb3Sn, NbTi, HTS) and RF heating or klystron sources, with cross-fertilised cryogenics and power systems.

name: Drift waves and Rossby waves
summary: Drift waves in magnetized plasma obey the Hasegawa–Mima equation, mathematically identical to the Charney–Hasegawa–Mima quasi-geostrophic equation, with zonal flows paralleling atmospheric jets.
breaks: Plasma drift waves involve adiabatic electron response and finite Larmor radius, with no direct atmospheric counterpart.

name: Planetary dynamos in Earth science
summary: Earth's field generation and reversals are a dynamo problem in rotating convecting conducting fluid, linking geophysics to MHD dynamo theory.

name: Rotating convective flows and quasi-geostrophy
summary: Core convection under rapid rotation is Taylor–Proudman constrained, mirroring geostrophic balance and Rossby-wave dynamics in the atmosphere, with Lorentz force replacing part of the Coriolis balance.
breaks: Magnetic field and Lorentz force alter the force balance (magnetostrophic), and there is no atmospheric analogue of induction.

name: Rotating stratified turbulence
summary: Ocean and core flows both exhibit rotation-dominated turbulence with inverse cascades and large-scale coherent structures, offering shared numerical and scaling tools.
breaks: Core flows are electrically conducting with Lorentz feedback, absent in oceans.

name: Geodynamo and the liquid outer core
summary: Earth's magnetic field is sustained by convective dynamo action in the liquid iron outer core, whose structure and inner-core growth are constrained by seismology.

name: Seismic constraints on dynamo core
summary: Seismic models give core radius, inner-core size and density jump, supplying boundary conditions and energy budget for geodynamo simulations.

name: Alfvén waves and Rossby waves
summary: Magnetic tension restoring Alfvén waves parallels the Coriolis restoring force of inertial and Rossby waves, and both reduce to similar dispersion structures in rotating or magnetized media.
breaks: Alfvén waves are non-dispersive, while Rossby and inertial waves are strongly dispersive and anisotropic differently.

name: Turbulent cascades in anisotropic media
summary: Anisotropic MHD cascades and quasi-2D geostrophic turbulence both develop strong anisotropy and inverse or dual transfers under a strong organizing field or rotation.
breaks: MHD has forward energy cascade in 3D with critical balance, differing from atmospheric inverse energy cascade.

name: Space charge and beam plasma physics
summary: Intense charged beams behave as non-neutral plasmas with Debye length, plasma frequency, space-charge tune shift and Coulomb-crystal ordering in cooled ion beams.
breaks: Beams are non-neutral and lack quasi-neutrality, so screening and collective response differ from true plasmas.

name: Vlasov description of beams
summary: Collective beam dynamics uses the Vlasov equation in phase space, with Landau damping of coherent modes via tune spread, equivalent to plasma Landau damping.

name: Beam instabilities as streaming instabilities
summary: Two-stream, Weibel and head-tail or microwave instabilities in beams share the kinetic-instability machinery of plasma physics, including Landau damping used to stabilise bunches.

name: Ionospheric and radiative propagation in plasma
summary: Electromagnetic wave propagation in ionised media, with plasma frequency cutoff, underlies ionospheric reflection and remote sensing, alongside atmospheric radiative physics.

name: Adiabatic invariants and magnetic focusing
summary: Gyration, mirror trapping and adiabatic invariants in plasma map onto betatron motion, Courant–Snyder invariants and magnetic confinement in storage rings and traps.
breaks: Accelerator lattices use alternating-gradient focusing with no plasma-style collective response.
